newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RESEARCH ALERT - Argentina's Molinos downgraded.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Argentina's Molinos downgraded.

text.p: -- Santander Investments said Monday it downgraded Molinos, Argentina's largest food producer and distributor, to "sell" from "market perform".

-- "Valuation is our main concern," analyst Arturo Torres wrote in a report. "The stock trades at 18 times our 1997 fully taxed earnings per share estimate, a 37 percent premium to the market and 38 percent premium to the average of its Latin American peers."
-- "We believe Molinos would be fairly valued at 15 times 1997 fully taxed earnings, resulting in a 12 to 18 months target price of $2.80 per share, 16 percent below the current market price.

-- "Most of Molinos sales come from already mature markets where compsumption per capita is not expected to grow further. The higly competitive environment and the increasing bargaining power of the retail industry have reduced the company's pricing ability.
-- "In addition most of Molinos's plants are running already at full capacity, with no near term plans to expand."
